findings.finding: Site was registered as a separate canonical entity and Site Assignment required siteId.
findings.resolution: Retain Site only as a legacy compatibility validator; OPLOC is the only publishable location identity; Site Assignment now references oplocId only.

findings.finding: Site was presented alongside OPLOC as a canonical definition.
findings.resolution: Expose definition status and label Site as a legacy source candidate.

findings.finding: Square locations are staged as Site and 18 matching records exist in staging and canonical candidate storage.
findings.resolution: Preserve existing records; add non-destructive OPLOC compatibility proposals and stop before changing IDs.

findings.finding: Site fields and required references assumed a separate location entity.
findings.resolution: Keep legacy transformation compatibility while preventing Site publication and new canonical use.

findings.finding: Source mappings used a generic target and publication did not gate every Future Candidate type.
findings.resolution: Location mappings require oplocId; publication eligibility requires Accepted Canon status.

findings.finding: Filters and columns described Site and OPLOC as peer identities.
findings.resolution: Use OPLOC terminology and present Site records as compatibility candidates.

findings.finding: Rota labels were mapped to a generic canonical Site target.
findings.resolution: Review only against existing OPLOCs or an explicit new OPLOC proposal.

findings.finding: Placement evidence and issue wording used Site labels where the source merely supplies location text.
findings.resolution: Use source location label and retain original evidence without canonical inference.

findings.finding: The prior readiness report recorded the conflict but did not state the now-authoritative correction.
findings.resolution: Supersede its location interpretation through the OPLOC alignment readiness report.

findings.finding: Historical supporting booking draft uses siteId.
findings.resolution: Do not silently rewrite; later governed booking revision should use OPLOC where current authority requires it.

findings.finding: No parentOplocId or OPLOC parent/child hierarchy exists.
Till and variation data remains outside active workflows.
The Domain Dictionary calls OPCAP canonical while CAP-001 metadata remains Draft.
findings.resolution: Do not implement the capability catalogue in this stage; retain the requirement for governed status reconciliation.
